lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: sorting clean from dirty

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 2 — clothing care and readiness routines
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice sorting clean from dirty. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner spreads a small pile of already-worn clothing across a bed or clear floor space, checks each item one at a time against the three specific tests, and places it into one of two labeled spots — a chair for 'clean enough' and a hamper or basket for 'needs washing' — before receiving any explicit teaching on the topic.
materials: learner-local: five or six already-worn clothing items
learner-local: a hamper, basket, or laundry bag
learner-local: a chair or clear spot for the 'clean enough' pile

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one specific item that looked clean at first glance but failed one of the three checks, or one that looked worn but actually passed all three.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Use of the three checks: Applies at least two of the three checks (stain, smell, wear count) consistently across the pile. | Sorting accuracy: Every item lands in a pile that matches the checks the learner described for it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the same three-check sort to the contents of a school backpack or gym bag, deciding which items inside need to go to the hamper and which can go back in the bag.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner spreads a small pile of already-worn clothing across a bed or clear floor space, checks each item one at a time against the three specific tests, and places it into one of two labeled spots — a chair for 'clean enough' and a hamper or basket for 'needs washing' — before receiving any explicit teaching on the topic.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact sorting clean from dirty decision or action.
Model move 2: Before sorting anything, look at the whole pile of worn clothing.
Model move 3: Pick up each item one at a time and run all three checks before placing it in a pile.

Model check: Use of the three checks: Applies at least two of the three checks (stain, smell, wear count) consistently across the pile. | Sorting accuracy: Every item lands in a pile that matches the checks the learner described for it.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for sorting clean from dirty.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner spreads a small pile of already-worn clothing across a bed or clear floor space, checks each item one at a time against the three specific tests, and places it into one of two labeled spots — a chair for 'clean enough' and a hamper or basket for 'needs washing' — before receiving any explicit teaching on the topic.
Coach direction: Before sorting anything, look at the whole pile of worn clothing.
Learner prompt: Guess how many of the items will end up in the 'needs washing' pile, and name the one item you are most sure about.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Pick up each item one at a time and run all three checks before placing it in a pile.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I checked each item for a visible stain or spot before deciding.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I checked the collar and underarm area of each item for a strong smell.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I thought about how many times the item has been worn since its last wash.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I placed every item into exactly one of the two piles, not left in the middle.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific item that looked clean at first glance but failed one of the three checks, or one that looked worn but actually passed all three.

Success checks: Use of the three checks: Applies at least two of the three checks (stain, smell, wear count) consistently across the pile. | Sorting accuracy: Every item lands in a pile that matches the checks the learner described for it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: sorting clean from dirty supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional sorting clean from dirty condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Use of the three checks: Applies at least two of the three checks (stain, smell, wear count) consistently across the pile. | Sorting accuracy: Every item lands in a pile that matches the checks the learner described for it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
